senses.gloss:
कंय्य कंय्य, अस्, आ, अम्, or कंय्यु, उस्, उस्, उ
(fr. 1. कम्), happy, prosperous; according to other
authorities also written कंय or कंयु or कंव.

कन्या, f. (the gen. pl. in Ṛg-veda is कनीनाम्),
a girl, a virgin, a daughter; (कन्यां दा or प्र-दा or
प्र-यम् or उप-पद् in Caus., to give one's daughter
in marriage; कन्याम् प्रति-ग्रह् or हृ or वह्, to
receive a girl in marriage, to marry); the sign of the
zodiac Virgo; an epithet of Durgā; N. of a metre
of four lines, each of them containing four long
syllables; an annual plant; N. of several plants, the
plant Aloe Perfoliata, a tuberous plant growing in
Kāśmīra; large cardamoms; [cf. Zend kainê; Hib.
cain, ‘chaste, undefiled;’ caile, ‘a country-woman,
a harlot;’ caileamhuil, ‘girlish, effeminate.’]
—कन्-
या-काल, अस्, m. the time of virginity.
—कन्या-
कुब्ज or कन्य-कुब्ज, अम्, n., N. of an ancient city
of great note, in the north of Hindūstan, situated on the
काली नदी, a branch of the Ganges, in the modern
district of Furruckabad. The popular spelling of the
name presents, perhaps, greater variations than that of
any place in India (e. g. Kunnoj, Kunnouj, Kinoge,
Kinnoge, Kinnauj, Kanoj, Kannauj, Kunowj,
Canowj, Canoje, Canauj, &c.). In antiquity this
city ranks next to Ayodhyā in Oude. It is known
to classical geography as Canogyza; but the name
applies also to its dependencies and the surrounding
district; the etymology (कन्या, a girl, and कुब्ज,
round-shouldered or crooked) refers to a legend relat-
ing to the hundred daughters of Kuśanābha, the king
of this city, who were all rendered crooked by Vāyu
for non-compliance with his licentious desires. The
ruins of the ancient city are said to occupy a site
larger than that of London.
—कन्याकुब्ज-देश,
अस्, m. the country round Kanyākubja.
—कन्या-
कुमारी or कन्य-कुमारि, इस्, f. the youthful god-
dess, an epithet of Durgā.
—कन्या-कूप, अस्, m.,
N. of a Tīrtha.
—कन्या-गत, अस्, आ, अम्, inhe-
rent in or pertaining to a virgin; the position of
a planet in the sign Virgo.
—कन्या-गर्भ,
अस्, m. the offspring of an unmarried woman.
—कन्या-ग्रहण, अम्, n. taking a girl in mar-
riage.
—कन्याट (˚या-आट), अस्, आ, अम्, follow-
ing after young girls; (अस्), m. the middle of a
house, the inner or private apartments for women.
—कन्या-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
—कन्या-
त्व, अम्, n. virginity.
—कन्या-दातृ, ता, m. a father
who gives a girl in marriage.
—कन्यादान (either
˚या-द्˚ or ˚या-आद्˚), अम्, n. giving a girl in mar-
riage; receiving a girl in marriage
—कन्या-दू-
षक, अस्, m. the violator or defiler of a virgin;
the calumniator of a girl.
—कन्या-दूषण, अम्,
n. defiling a virgin, calumniating a girl.
—कन्या-
दोष, अस्, m. a blemish in a virgin, disease, bad
repute, &c.
—कन्या-धन, अम्, n. a portion,
dowry.
—कन्या-पति, इस्, m. a daughter's husband.
—कन्या-पाल, अस्, m. a dealer in slave girls; the
father of a maiden; [cf. कल्या-पाल.]
—कन्या-
पुत्र, अस्, m. the offspring of an unmarried daughter.
—कन्या-पुर, अम्, n. the women's apartments.
—कन्या-प्रदान, अम्, n. giving a daughter in
marriage.
—कन्या-भर्तृ or कन्या-हर्तृ (?) , ता,
m. an epithet of Kārttikeya.
—कन्या-भाव, अस्, m.
virginity.
—कन्या-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting in a
girl (as property &c.), being a girl.
—कन्या-रत्न,
अम्, n. a jewel of a damsel, a lovely girl.
—कन्या-
राम, अस्, m., N. of a Buddha.
—कन्या-राशि, इस्,
m. the sign Virgo.
—कन्या-वेदिन्, ई, m. a son-in-law.
—कन्या-शुल्क, अम्, n. the purchase-money of a
maiden, money given to the bride's father.
—कन्या-
श्रम (˚या-आश्˚), अस्, m., N. of a hermitage.
—कन्या-संवेद्य, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
—कन्या-समुद्भव, अस्, m. the son of an un-
married girl.
—कन्या-सम्प्रदान, अम्, n. the
giving away a maiden in marriage.
—कन्या-स्व-
यंवर, अस्, m. the choice of a husband by a
[]
maiden.
—कन्या-हरण, अम्, n. carrying off a
girl, rape, ravishment.
—कन्या-ह्रद, अस्, m., N.
of a Tīrtha.

कंवूल कंवूल or कवूल, अम्, n., N. of
the eighth Yoga, = Arabic قبول
कंश कंश, अस्, अम्, m. n. = कंस, q. v.

कंस कंस, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt.
2. कम्; according to others fr. the last), a vessel
made of metal, a drinking vessel, a cup, a goblet (a
noun ending in अस् followed by कंस in a compound
does not change its final, e. g. अयस्-कंस, पयस्-
[]
कंस, &c.); a particular measure; a metal, tutanag
or white copper, brass, bell-metal; cf. कंसास्थि and
कांस्य; (अस्), m., N. of a king of Mathurā, son of
Ugra-sena and cousin of the Devakī who was mother
of Kṛṣṇa, (Ugra-sena being brother of Devaka, who
was father of Devakī.) He is usually called the uncle,
but was really a cousin of Kṛṣṇa, and became his
implacable enemy because it had been prophesied to
him that he would be killed by a child of Devakī
(Vish. Pur. p. 493); as the foe of the deity he is
identified with the Asura Kālanemi; and, as he was
ultimately slain by Kṛṣṇa, the latter receives epithets
like कंस-जित्, the conqueror of Kaṃsa, &c.; (आ), f.
N. of a daughter of Ugra-sena and sister of Kaṃsa.
—कंस-कार, अस्, ई, m. f. a worker in pewter or
white brass, a bell-founder, considered as an inter-
mediate caste.
—कंस-जित्, त्, m. an epithet of
Kṛṣṇa, the conqueror of Kaṃsa.
—कंस-बणिज्, क्,
m. a brazier or seller of brass vessels.
—कंस-
बध, अस्, m. the slaying of Kṛṣṇa; title of a
comedy of Śeṣa-Kṛṣṇa.
—कंस-माक्षिक, अम्,
n. a metallic substance in large grains, a sort of
pyrites.
—कंस-यज्ञ, अस्, m. a particular sacrifice.
—कंस-वती, f., N. of a daughter of Ugra-sena and
sister of Kaṃsa and Kaṃsā.
—कंस-हन्, आ, m. an
epithet of Kṛṣṇa, the destroyer of Kaṃsa.
—कंस-
हनन, अम्, n. the slaying of Kaṃsa.
—कंसाराति
(˚स-अर्˚), इस्, or कंसारि (˚स-अरि), इस्, m. epithet
of Kṛṣṇa, the enemy of Kaṃsa.
—कंसास्थि (˚स-
अस्˚), इ, n. tutanag, white copper, any alloy of tin and
copper.
—कंसोद्भवा (˚स-उद्˚), f. a fragrant earth.
कांस कांस, अस्, ई, अम्, born in Kaṃsa.

कंस् कंस्, cl. 2. A. कंस्ते, -सितुम्, to go;
to command; to destroy. See कस्.

कांस् कांस्, cl. 1. A. कांसते, -सितुम्, to
shine, glitter; [cf. काश्.]

कंसक, अम्, n. a mineral substance, a salt of
iron used as an application to the eyes.
कंसिक, अस्, ई, अम्, made of bell-metal &c.

कंसीय, अस्, आ, अम्, fit for or relating to a cup;
(अम्), n. bell-metal.

कांसीय कांसीय, अम्, n. white copper; [cf.
the following.]

कंसार कं-सार, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (rice) the
grain of which hardens in the centre.

कन् कन्, cl. 1. P., Ved. कनति, चकान,
अकानीत्, कन्तुम् (of the simple root only
the aor. is used), to be satisfied; to be contented
with, to accept anything (acc.) with satisfaction;
(Sāy.) to love, wish, desire; to shine; to go: Intens.
चाकन्ति, impf. चाकन्, perf. चाकन and चके, to be
satisfied, to like, enjoy anything (with loc., gen.); to
inst.); to be liked, wished, desired (with gen.); to
strive after, seek, desire (with acc. or dat.); [cf. कम्
and चन्: cf. also Lat. canus, caneo, candeo, can-
dela; Hib. canu, ‘full moon.’]

कन कन, a substitute for अल्प, little,
small, not occurring alone, but regarded as the source
of the following derivatives; [cf. कण.]
कना, f., Ved. a girl.

कनय, nom. P. कनयति, -यितुम्, to make
less or smaller, diminish.

कनिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, the smallest, least (opposed
to भूयिष्ठ); the youngest, younger born (opposed
to ज्येष्ठ and वृद्ध); (आ), f. (with or without
अङ्गुलिः) the little finger; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a class
of deities of the fourteenth Manvantara; (आ), f. a
kind of heroine.
—कनिष्ठ-ता, f. or कनिष्ठ-
त्व, अम्, n. the state of being younger or smaller.
—कनिष्ठ-पद or कनिष्ठ-मूल, अम्, n.
the least or first root; that quantity of which the
square multiplied by the given multiplicator and
having the given addend added or subtrahend sub-
tracted is capable of affording an exact square root.

कनिष्ठ, कनी, कनीन, कनीयस्। See under
कन.

कनिष्ठक, अस्, इका, अम्, Ved. the smallest;
(आ), f. the little finger; (अम्), n. a kind of grass.
कनी, f. a girl, a maiden.

कनीन, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. young; (ई), f. the pupil
of the eye; the little finger.

कानीन कानीन, अस्, ई, m. f. (fr. कनीन),
the son or daughter of a young or unmarried woman;
an epithet of Vyāsa, Karṇa, and Agniveśya; (अस्, आ,
अम्), suitable to or designed for the eye-ball; [cf.
कनीनक.]

कनीनक, अस्, m. a boy, a youth; the pupil of
the eye; the caruncula lacrymalis; (आ), f. a maiden,
a young girl, a virgin; the pupil of the eye; (इका),
f. the pupil of the eye; the little finger.

कनीयस्, आन्, असी, अस् (opposed to भूयस्, ज्यायस्,
[]
उत्तम), smaller, less; younger, a younger brother
or sister, a younger son or daughter.

कनीयस, अस्, आ, अम्, smaller, less; younger;
(अम्), n. copper (‘of less value’); [cf. कन्यस.]

कानीयस (fr. कनीयस्), less in number (used
only in plur.).
कन्यका, कन्या. See s. v.

कन्यका कन्यका, f. (see कन), a girl, a
[]
maiden; a young virgin; a daughter; the constellation
Virgo in the zodiac; the plant Aloe Perfoliata.
—कन्-
यका-गुण, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
—कन्यका-
छल, अम्, n. beguiling a maiden, seduction, betrayal.
—कन्यका-जन, अस्, m. a maiden.
—कन्यका-
जात, अस्, m. the son of an unmarried woman.
—कन्यका-पति, इस्, m. a daughter's husband.
कन्याका or कन्यिका, f. a young girl, a virgin.

कनक कनक, अम्, n. (said to be fr. rt. कन्),
gold; N. of several plants, Datura Metel and Fastuosa,
thorn apple; Mesua Ferrea; Michelia Champaka;
Butea Frondosa; Bauhinia Variegata; a black sort
of Agallochum or sandal-wood; (अस्), m., N. of a
prince, a son of Durdama; N. of a son of a goddess;
N. of a minister of Narendrāditya; (आस्), m. pl., N.
of a people; (आ), f. one of the seven tongues of fire.
—कनक-कुण्डला, f. the mother of Harikeśa.
—कनक-क्षर, अस्, m. borax.
—कनक-गिरि,
इस्, m., N. of the founder of a sect.
—कनक-टङ्क,
अस्, m. a golden hatchet.
—कनक-तालाभ (˚ल-
आभा), अस्, आ, अम्, bright as a golden palm tree.
—कनक-दण्डक, अस्, m. the royal parasol
(golden-sticked).
—कनक-दत्त, अस्, m. the son
of Nidhipati.
—कनक-ध्वज, अस्, m., N. of a son
of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra.
—कनक-पराग, अस्, m. gold-
dust.
—कनक-पल, अस्, m. a Pala, a weight of
gold and silver equal to sixteen Māṣakas, or about
280 grains troy.
—कनक-पिङ्गल, N. of a Tīrtha.
—कनक-पुर, अम्, ई, n. f., N. of a town.
—क-
नक-प्रभा, f., N. of a plant; N. of a metre con-
sisting of four lines of thirteen syllables each; N. of
a princess; (अस्, आ, अम्), bright as gold.
—कनक-
प्रसवा, f., N. of a plant.
—कनक-भङ्ग, अस्,
m. a piece of gold.
—कनक-मय, अस्, ई, अम्,
golden, consisting or made of gold.
—कनक-
मुनि, इस्, m., N. of a Buddha.
—कनक-रम्भा,
f., N. of a plant.
—कनक-रस, अस्, m. fluid
gold; a yellow orpiment.
—कनक-रेखा, f., N. of
a daughter of Kanaka-prabhā.
—कनकलोद्भव,
अस्, m. (fr. कनक-कल-उद्भव ?), resin of the
plant Shorea Robusta.
—कनक-वती, f., N. of the
residence of king Kanaka-varṇa; [cf. कनका-वती.]
—कनक-वर्ण, अस्, m., N. of a king supposed to
be a former manifestation of Śākya-muni.
—कनक-
वाहिनी, f., N. of a river (‘gold stream’).
—कनक-
विग्रह, अस्, m., N. of a king of Viśālapurī.
—क-
नक-शक्ति, इस्, m. an epithet of Kārttikeya; [cf.
शक्ति-धर.]
—कनक-सूत्र, अम्, n. a gold
cord.
—कनक-स्तम्भ-रुचिर, अस्, आ, अम्, shin-
ing with columns of gold.
—कनक-स्थली, f. a gold
mine, golden soil.
—कनकाङ्गद (˚क-अन्˚), अस्,
m., N. of a son of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra.
—कनकाचल
(˚क-अच्˚), अस्, m. the golden mountain; an epithet
of the mountain Sumeru.
—कनकाद्रि-खण्ड
(˚क-अद्˚), अम्, n. a section of the Skanda-purāṇa.
—कनकाध्यक्ष (˚क-अध्˚), अस्, m. the trea-
surer or superintendent of the gold.
—कनकायु
(˚क-आयु), उस्, m., N. of a son of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; (a
various reading has करकायु.)
—कनकालुका (˚क-
आल्˚), f. a golden jar or vase.
—कनका-वती, f. a
proper name.
—कनकावती-माधव, अस्, m. title
of a work.
—कनकाह्व (˚क-आह्˚), अम्, n. the
blossom of the tree Mesua Ferrea.
—कनकाह्वय,
अस्, m. the thorn apple; Mesua Ferrea; N. of a
Buddha.
—कनकेश्वर-तीर्थ (˚क-ईश्˚), अम्, n.,
N. of a Tīrtha.

कानक कानक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. कनक),
golden; (अम्), n. the seed of Croton Jamalgota.

कनकारक, अस्, m. the tree Bauhinia Variegata
Lin.; [cf. काञ्चनार and कान्तार.]

कनक्नक कनक्नक, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. epithet
of a kind of poison.

कनखल कनखल, अम्, n. and (आस्), m. pl.,
N. of a Tīrtha and the mountains surrounding it.
कनटी कनटी, f. red arsenic, = कुनटी.

कनदेव कनदेव, अस्, m., N. of a Buddhist
patriarch.
कनन कनन, अस्, आ, अम्, one-eyed; [cf. काण.]

कानन 1. कानन, अम्, n. (said to be fr. rt.
कन्), a forest, grove; a house.
—काननारि (˚न-
अरि), इस्, m. a species of the Mimosa tree, Śamī.
—काननौकस् (˚न-ओक्˚), आस्, m. the inhabitant of
a forest, a monkey; [cf. वनौकस्.]

कानन 2. कानन (क-आन्˚), अम्, n. the face
of Brahmā.

कनप कनप, a various reading for क-
णप, q. v.
कनवक कनवक, अस्, m., N. of a son of Śūra.
कनाठ कनाठ, अस्, m., N. of a man.

कनिक्रद कनिक्रद, अस्, आ, अम् (an Intens.
form of rt. क्रन्द्), Ved. neighing.

कनिष्क कनिष्क, अस्, m., N. of an Indo-
scythic king, celebrated in the history of Buddhism.
—कनिष्क-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town founded
by Kaniṣka.

कनीचि कनीचि, इस्, f. a cart; a creeping plant
with blossoms; the plant Abrus Precatorius.

कनूज कनूज, a corruption of कन्या-कुब्ज,
q. v.
—कनूज-देश, अस्, m. the country round
Kanyā-kubja.

कनेरा कनेरा, f. a female elephant; a
harlot. See कणेरा.

कन्त कन्त, अस्, आ, अम्, or कन्ति, इस्, इस्, इ (fr.
1. कम्), happy.

कान्त कान्त, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. 2. कम्), desired,
loved, dear; pleasing, agreeable; lovely, beautiful;
(अस्), m. a lover, a husband; any one beloved; the
moon; spring; the plant Barringtonia Acutangula
[cf. हिज्जल]; iron; stone; a precious stone (in
[]
which sense it is compounded with सूर्य, चन्द्र,
and अयस्); an epithet of Kṛṣṇa, and of Skanda;
(आ), f. a beloved or lovely woman, a wife, a mistress;
the earth; N. of a plant (commonly called प्रियङ्गु);
also of another plant (= नागर-मुस्ता); large car-
damoms; a kind of perfume (see रेणुका); N. of a
metre of four lines of seventeen syllables each; (अम्),
n. saffron; a species of iron.
—कान्त-ता, f. or
कान्त-त्व, अम्, n. loveliness, beauty, agreeableness.
—कान्त-पक्षिन्, ई, m. a peacock (‘the beautiful
bird’).
—कान्त-पुष्प, अस्, m. the tree Bauhinia
Variegata, mountain ebony.
—कान्त-मिश्र, अस्, m.,
N. of a man.
—कान्त-लोह, अम्, n. the loadstone.
—कान्त-लौह, अस् or अम् (?), m. or n. steel; [cf.
लोह-कान्त.]
—कान्ताङ्घ्रि-दोहद (˚ता-अङ्˚), अस्,
m. the tree Jonesia Aśoka (this tree being supposed to
blossom upon coming in contact with the foot of a
handsome female).
—कान्ता-चरण-दोहद, अस्, m.
= the preceding.
—कान्तायस (˚त-अयस्), अम्, n. the
iron stone; [cf. कान्त-लोह and अयस्-कान्त.]

कन्तु, उस्, उस्, उ, happy; (उस्), m. the heart as
the seat or faculty of perception and feeling; Kāma-
deva, the deity of love; a granary.
कन्थक कन्थक, अस्, m., N. of a man.

कान्थक कान्थक fr. कन्था, N. of a place
on the river Varṇu.

कन्थरी कन्थरी, f., N. of a tree. See कन्-
था, कन्थारी, क्रूरगन्धा, तीक्ष्णकण्टका, &c.
कन्थारी कन्थारी, f., N. of a tree.

कन्था कन्था, f. a rag, a patched garment,
especially one worn by certain ascetics; a wall; a
town (in composition the word is neuter if the com-
pound imply a town of the Uśīnāras); a kind of
tree; N. of a country.
—कन्था-धारण, अम्, n.
wearing a patched garment as practised by certain
Yogis.
—कन्था-धारिन्, ई, इणी, m. f. a Yogi, a
religious mendicant.
—कन्थेश्वर-तीर्थ (˚था-
ईश्˚), अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.

कन्द् कन्द्, cl. 1. P. कन्दति, -दितुम्, to
cry, utter lamentations; A. कन्दते, to be
confounded, confound; [cf. 1. कद्, क्रन्द्, क्लन्द्.]

कन्द कन्द, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt.
कन्), a bulbous or tuberous root; a bulb; the bulb-
ous root of Amorphophallus Campanulatus; garlic;
a lump, swelling, knot; an affection of the feminine
organ, considered as a fleshy excrescence, but ap-
parently prolapsus uteri; N. of a metre of four lines
of thirteen syllables each; a cloud (in this sense fr.
कम्, water, and द).
—कन्द-गुडूची, f., N. of a
plant, = कन्द-रोहिणी, &c.
—कन्द-ज, अस्, आ, अम्,
growing from bulbs.
—कन्द-द, अस्, आ, अम्, giving
or forming bulbs.
—कन्द-फला, f., N. of a plant.
—कन्द-बहुला, f., N. of a plant.
—कन्द-मूल,
अम्, n. a radish.
—कन्द-लता, f., N. of a plant
with a bulbous root.
—कन्द-वत्, आन्, m. a species
of the Soma plant.
—कन्द-वर्धन, अस्, m.
the esculent root of Amorphophallus Campanulatus.
—कन्द-वल्ली, f., N. of a plant.
—कन्द-शूरण,
अस्, m. the plant Amorphophallus Campanulatus.
—कन्द-सञ्ज्ञ, अम्, n. prolapsus uteri; [cf.
कन्द.]
—कन्द-सम्भव, अस्, आ, अम्, growing
from bulbs.
—कन्द-सार, अम्, n. the garden or
grove of Indra.
—कन्दाढ्य, (˚द-आढ्˚), अस्, m.
a kind of tuberous plant.
—कन्दामृता (˚द-अम्˚),
f., N. of a plant, = कन्द-गुडूची.
—कन्दार्ह
(˚द-अर्˚), अस्, m. the plant Amorphophallus Cam-
panulatus.
—कन्दोद्भवा (˚द-उद्˚), f., N. of a
plant, = कन्द-गुडूची.

कन्दालु, उस्, m., N. of several plants; an escu-
lent root; a sort of Arum &c.

कन्दिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having a bulbous root; (ई), m.
the plant Amorphophallus Campanulatus.

कन्दक कन्दक, अस्, m. a palanquin, =
कदक.

कन्दट कन्दट, अम्, n. the white esculent
water-lily; [cf. कन्दोट and कन्दोत.]

कन्दर कन्दर, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, m. f. n.
(perhaps fr. कम्-दर), an artificial or natural cave;
a glen, a defile, a valley; (अस्), m. a hook for driving
an elephant; (अम्), n. dry ginger (in this sense fr.
कन्द, ‘consisting of bulbs’?).
—कन्दर-वत्,
आन्, अती, अत्, containing caves or valleys (as a moun-
tain).
—कन्दराकार (˚र-आक्˚), अस्, m. a moun-
tain.
—कन्दरान्तर (˚र-अन्˚), अम्, n. the interior
of a cave.
—कन्दराल (˚र-आल = आलय), अस्, m.,
N. of several plants, Hibiscus Populneoides; Ficus
Infectoria.
—कन्दरालक, अस्, m. the tree Ficus
Infectoria.
—कन्दरोद्भवा (˚र-उद्˚), f., N. of a
plant.

कन्दर्प कन्दर्प, अस्, m. (fr. कम्-दर्प,
‘how haughty;’ or, according to others, ‘the in-
flamer even of the chief of gods;’ see 3. क), N.
of the deity Kāma, or the god of love, the Cupid of
the Hindū mythology; love; (आ), f. one of the pre-
siding female deities of the Jainas executing the
orders of the fifteenth Arhat.
—कन्दर्प-कूप,
अस्, m. pudendum muliebre, (‘a well of love.’)
—कन्दर्प-केतु, उस्, m., N. of a prince.
—कन्-
दर्प-केलि, इस्, m. title of a work.
—कन्दर्प-
जीव, अस्, m., N. of a plant, = काम-वृद्धि.
—कन्-
दर्प-ज्वर, अस्, m. passion, desire.
—कन्दर्प-
दहन, अम्, n. a section of the Śiva-purāṇa.
—कन्दर्प-मुसल, अस्, m. membrum virile.
—कन्दर्प-शृङ्खल, अस्, m. a kind of coitus.
—कन्दर्प-सिद्धान्त, अस्, m., N. of a scholiast
on Supadma.

कन्दल कन्दल, अस्, आ, अम्, m. f. n. the skull
(= कपाल); the cheek, or the cheek and temple;
a new shoot or sprig; a low soft tone; a portent, a
natural phenomenon supposed to forbode evil; re-
proach, censure; (अस्), m. gold; war, battle; (ई), f.
a species of deer of which the hide is used; a plant,
the plantain tree or banana tree (Musa Sapientum;
see कदली); lotus seed; a flag, a banner; (अम्), n.
the flower of Musa Sapientum; perhaps a mushroom.
—कन्दली-कार, अस्, m., N. of an author.
—कन्-
दली-कुसुम, अम्, n. a mushroom.

कन्दलित, अस्, आ, अम्, covered with mushrooms (?) ;
budded, blown; put forth, emitted.

कन्दलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, covered with mushrooms;
(ई), m. a kind of antelope (?) .

कन्दिरी कन्दिरी, f. the plant Mimosa
Pudica.

कन्दु कन्दु, उस्, m. f. (said to be fr. rt.
स्कन्द्), a boiler, a saucepan, or other cooking
utensil of iron; an oven, or vessel serving for one;
(उस्), m., N. of a Muni.
—कन्दु-पक्व, अस्, आ, अम्,
parched, roasted (as grain), fried &c. in a pan, dressed
without water.

कन्दुक कन्दुक, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be
fr. the preceding), a ball of wood or pith for playing
with; (अम्), n. a pillow; a germ (?) .
—कन्दुक-
प्रस्थ, अस्, m., N. of a town.
—कन्दुक-लीला, f.
any game with a ball, fives.
—कन्दुकेश (˚क-ईश),
अस्, m., N. of a man.
—कन्दुकेश्वर-लिङ्ग (˚क-
ईश्˚), अम्, n., N. of a Liṅga.

कन्दोट कन्दोट, अस्, m. the white lotus,
Nymphæa Esculenta; (अम्), n. the blue lotus.

कन्दोत, अस्, m. the white lotus, Nymphæa Escu-
lenta. See कन्दट.

कन्ध कन्-ध, अस्, m. (fr. कम्, water, and
ध fr. rt. धा), a cloud.

कन्-धर, अस्, आ, m. f. (fr. कम्, head, and
धर fr. rt. धृ), the neck; (अस्), m. the plant
Amaranthus Oleraceus; (कम् = water), a cloud.

कन्-धि, इस्, m. (fr. कम्, water, and धि fr. rt.
धा), the ocean; (इस्), f. (कम् = head), the neck.
कन्यना or कन्यला, f., Ved. a girl.

कन्यस कन्यस, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. कनीयस्),
younger; (आ), f. the little finger.

कन्युष कन्युष, अम्, n. the hand below
the wrist.
कांशि कांशि, इस्, m. a cup; [cf. कांस्य.]

कांस्य कांस्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. कंस), con-
sisting of white copper or brass; (अम्), n. white
copper or brass, queen's metal, any amalgam of zinc
and copper; a musical instrument, a sort of gong or
plate of bell-metal struck with a stick or rod; a kind
of measure; (अस्, अम्), m. n. a drinking vessel of brass,
a goblet.
—कांस्य-कार, अस्, ई, m. f. a brazier, a
pewterer, a worker in white or bell-metal.
—कांस्य-
ज, अस्, आ, अम्, made of brass.
—कांस्य-ताल, अस्, m.
[]
a cymbal.
—कांस्य-नील, अस्, m. blue vitriol con-
sidered as a collyrium; N. of a monkey; occasionally
written कांश्य-नील.
—कांस्य-भाजन, अम्, n.
brass.
—कांस्य-मय, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting or made
of brass.
—कांस्य-मल, अम्, n. verdigris.
—कांस्य-
माक्षिक, अम्, n. a metallic substance, probably a
kind of pyrites.
—कांस्याभ (˚य-आभ), अस्, आ, अम्,
coloured like brass.
कांस्यक, अम्, n. brass.

कानद कानद, अस्, m., N. of a son of
Dhīmarana.

कानीत कानीत, अस्, m. a patronymic of
Pṛthu-śravas.
कान्तक, अस्, m., N. of a man.

कान्तलक, अस्, m. the tree Cedrela Toona, com-
monly Tunna, the wood of which sometimes resembles
mahogany.

कान्ताय, nom. A. -यते, -यितुम्, to behave like
a lover.

कान्ति, इस्, f. desire, wish; loveliness, beauty;
splendor; female beauty; personal decoration or
embellishment; (in rhetoric) beauty enhanced by
love; a lovely or desirable woman, personified as
wife of the moon.
—कान्ति-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, causing
beauty, beautifying, illuminating.
—कान्ति-द, अस्, आ,
अम्, giving beauty; beautifying, adorning; (आ), f.
the plant Serratula Anthelmintika; (अम्), n. bile,
the bilious humor.
—कान्ति-दायक, अस्, इका, अम्,
granting beauty; beautifying, adorning; (अम्), n. a
fragrant wood, a kind of Curcuma from the root of
which a yellow die is prepared, C. Zanthorrhiza.
—कान्ति-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town in Nepal.
—कान्ति-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, lovely, beautiful, splen-
did; (ती), f., N. of a metre; N. of a woman.
—कान्ति-
मत्-ता, f. loveliness, beauty.
—कान्ति-हर, अस्, ई,
अम्, destroying beauty, making ugly, dulling, dim-
ming.
—कान्ती-नगरी, f. (for कान्ति-न्˚), N. of a
city of the north; [cf. कान्ति-पुर].
कान्तिक, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.

कान्तार कान्तार, अस्, अम्, m. n. a wood or
large forest; a bad or difficult road; a hole, a cavity;
(अस्), m. a red variety of the sugar-cane; a bamboo;
mountain ebony, Bauhinia Variegata; (ई), f. a kind
of sugar-cane; (अम्), n. a symptom or symptomatic
disease, a lotus.
—कान्तार-ग, अस्, आ, अम्, who or
what goes into a wood.
—कान्तार-पथ, अस्, m.
a forest-way.
—कान्तार-पथिक, अस्, ई, अम्, con-
veyed on difficult forest roads.
—कान्तार-वासिनी, f.
an epithet of Durgā.

कान्तारक, अस्, m. a kind of sugar-cane; (आस्),
m. pl., N. of a people; (इका), f. a kind of bee.

कान्तोत्पाडा कान्तोत्पाडा, f. (for कान्तोत्पा-
दा?), N. of a metre consisting of four lines of twelve
syllables each.

कान्दव कान्दव, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. कन्दु),
roasted or baked, in an iron pan or oven, as bread,
cakes, &c.

कान्दविक, अस्, ई, अम्, employed in baking;
(अस्), m. a baker.

कान्दाविष कान्दा-विष, अम्, n., Ved. a
species of poison.

कान्दिश् कान्दिश्, क्, क्, क्, or कान्दिशीक, अस्, आ,
अम्, put to flight, running away, flying; (fr. कां
दिशम्, ‘to which region’ shall I fly?).
—कान्दिग्-
भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, run away.

कान्यकुब्ज कान्यकुब्ज, अम्, n. = कन्य-
कुब्ज, N. of a town; (ई), f. a princess or a female
inhabitant of this town.

कान्यजा कान्यजा, f. a kind of perfume,
commonly Nālī.

कानिष्ठ्य, अम्, n. (fr. कनिष्ठ), the place
or position of the youngest (opposed to ज्यैष्ठ्य),
juniority.
